name: Yala Peak Climbing
sub_region: Rasuwa District (Langtang National Park, near the Tibet border north-east of Kyanjin Gompa), Bagmati Province

difficulty.notes: Relatively non-technical snow/rock ascent: snow slopes and scrambling, with a short steep rock pyramid near the top where hands are needed. Crampons and ice axe used; harness/helmet recommended. Good first Himalayan summit. [s6, s7, s8]

duration_days.notes: Operators sell 10-16 days. Climb takes 2-3 days from Kyanjin Gompa via a high camp at Yala Kharka, with a spare weather day; can be done in one long day from Kyanjin. Since the Aug 2026 flood the walk starts from Dhunche/Thulo Syabru (see langtang-valley-trek). [s6, s7, s9, s10]

max_altitude_point: Yala Peak summit - UNVERIFIED height (5,732 m in NMA/MoCTCA lists; 5,500-5,520 m in many guides)

itinerary.route: Kyanjin Gompa - Yala Kharka / high camp
itinerary.notes: High camp given as 4,600-4,800 m (one operator 4,940 m). [s6, s7, s9]

itinerary.route: Summit Yala Peak, descend to Kyanjin Gompa
itinerary.notes: Pre-dawn start; summit views include Shishapangma (8,013 m) in Tibet. [s6, s7]

best_seasons.notes: See langtang-valley-trek for the 2026 flood access situation. [s12]

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500; under 10 free)

permits.name: TIMS card (agency-issued e-TIMS)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals; Langtang Trek is on NTB's guide + TIMS list

permits.name: NMA climbing royalty
permits.fee: Royalty waived (USD 0): per operators, a Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation decision made NMA peaks below 5,800 m (Yala, Chhukung Ri, Tent Peak, Mardi Himal, Machhermo, Pokhalde) royalty-free. Yala is absent from NMA's current 27-peak fee table.

permits.name: Garbage deposit
permits.fee: Reported as USD 500 per group (one operator); older NMA rule cited USD 250 for NMA peaks

permits.name: Langtang NP camping fee (if camping at high camp)
permits.fee: Reported NPR 1,500 per night for foreigners (one operator)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals camping in the park

guide_requirements: Licensed trekking guide and agency-issued TIMS card required in Langtang (NTB, 31 March 2023 provision); a licensed climbing guide is used for the summit. [s2, s9]

drives: Kathmandu - Trishuli - Betrawati - Dhunche - Syabrubesi: approx. 7-9 hours (Betrawati Bailey bridge reopened 11 Oct 2026)
logistics.notes: Teahouses to Kyanjin Gompa; tented high camp at Yala Kharka. [s6, s7]

highlights: Accessible first Himalayan summit above 5,000 m
Summit views of Shishapangma (8,013 m) and Langtang peaks
Often used as a warm-up for Naya Kanga (Ganja La Chuli)
risks: Snow, ice and loose rock; exposed final rock pyramid

acclimatization.notes: At least one acclimatization day at Kyanjin before moving to high camp. [s9]

unverified: Summit height: 5,732 m (NMA/MoCTCA royalty-free list, historical NMA) vs 5,500-5,520 m (Wikipedia per one source, many operators).
Royalty-free status: multiple operators cite a MoCTCA decision; no government notice was found directly, though Yala is absent from NMA's current 27-peak fee table.
Garbage deposit amount for Yala (USD 500 per group vs USD 250).
Langtang NP camping fee of NPR 1,500/night (single operator).
